canonicalExplanation.summary: When content is bigger than its box, `overflow` decides what happens: `visible` (spills out — the default), `hidden` (clips it, possibly hiding important content), `auto` (adds a scrollbar only when needed), or `scroll`. `overflow: hidden` is not a universal fix — it can cut off text, focus outlines and dropdowns. Prefer letting content **wrap** or **scroll deliberately**, and make scroll areas reachable by keyboard.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A tutorial shows long lines of code. On a phone they burst out of the page, so someone adds `overflow: hidden` to the body — now the end of each line is simply gone, along with a menu that opened past the edge. A code sample uses overflow:auto and remains keyboard-scrollable without clipping long lines permanently. In this lesson you'll repair overflow across narrow, zoomed and long-content scenarios.

```predict
{"question": "`overflow: hidden` on a card with a long word inside. Can users read the whole word?", "options": ["Yes, it wraps automatically", "No — the part outside the box is clipped and unreachable"], "answer": 1, "why": "hidden cuts content off. Users can't scroll to it, and focus rings or menus near the edge get clipped too."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Rules, declarations and values**, **Intrinsic sizing and constraints**, and **Pseudo-classes and pseudo-elements** (focus styles can be clipped by overflow).

sections.heading: The model: spill, clip or scroll
sections.body:
```css pre { overflow-x: auto; /* horizontal scrollbar only when needed */ max-width: 100%; } pre:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #f59e0b; } .prose { overflow-wrap: anywhere; } /* long words wrap instead */ ``` ```html 
…long lines…
``` | Value | Effect | Risk | |---|---|---| | `visible`. | content spills out. | overlaps other content. | | `hidden`. | clips. | hides content, focus rings, menus. | | `auto`. | scrollbar when needed. | needs keyboard access. | | `clip`. | clips, no scrolling at all. | same as hidden, stricter. | ```reveal {"prompt": "Why add `tabindex=\"0\"` to a scrollable pre?", "answer": "So keyboard users can focus it and scroll with arrow keys. Some browsers make scroll containers focusable automatically; adding it (with a label) makes it reliable."} ```

sections.heading: Test three scenarios

includes: Choose overflow values and prefer wrapping or deliberate scrolling over clipping.
Keep scroll areas keyboard-accessible and test narrow, zoomed and long content.

outcomes: Repair overflow across narrow, zoomed and long-content scenarios.

examples.title: A scrollable code sample
examples.situation: A code sample uses overflow:auto and remains keyboard-scrollable without clipping long lines permanently.
walkthrough: **Problem:** long code lines burst out of the page at 320px wide; a global `overflow: hidden` had been clipping them.
**Fix:** remove the global hidden; `pre { overflow-x: auto }` adds a scrollbar only when needed.
**Keyboard:** `tabindex="0"` plus a focus style lets keyboard users focus the block and read long lines with the arrow keys.
examples.result: Every character of the code is reachable by mouse, touch and keyboard, and the page no longer scrolls sideways.

examples.title: The clipped dropdown
examples.situation: A card with `overflow: hidden` (added to crop a rounded image) contains a menu. When opened, the menu is cut off at the card's edge.
walkthrough: overflow: hidden clips all descendants, including the menu.
Users can't reach the lower menu items.
Fix: remove hidden from the card; round the image itself with `border-radius`, or clip only the image wrapper.
examples.result: The menu opens fully while the image stays neatly rounded.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: overflow:hidden is a safe universal fix for any layout that becomes too large.
misconceptions.correction: hidden clips content, focus indicators and popups, making them unreachable. Fix the cause — allow wrapping, lift min-size constraints, or scroll deliberately with overflow:auto and keyboard access.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The clipped dropdown", what else did overflow:hidden cut off?

analogy.example: overflow: hidden is like **cutting a poster to fit a small frame** — the edges are gone for good. overflow: auto is like a **scroll** you can unroll. Wrapping is folding the text so it fits properly.
limitations: Posters don't have focus rings or menus that also get cut.
A scroll must be reachable by keyboard, not just a mouse wheel.

steps.explanation: The global hidden fix clipped long lines permanently.
The code sample uses overflow:auto instead.

nearTransfer.prompt: A table is wider than the phone screen. How do you let users see all columns without the whole page scrolling sideways?
scaffold: Wrap it in a scroll container.
expectedEvidence: A wrapper div with overflow-x: auto around the table.
tabindex="0", a label and a visible focus style on the wrapper.

farTransfer.prompt: Audit a page for every `overflow: hidden`. For each, decide whether it clips anything important at 320px, 200% zoom and with long text; replace harmful ones.
expectedEvidence: List of each hidden with a decision.

remediation.explanation: Before adding overflow: hidden, ask: **What will be cut off at 320px, at 200% zoom, with twice the text?** If anything important, choose wrapping or overflow: auto instead.

recap.summary: To repair overflow across narrow, zoomed and long-content scenarios, prefer wrapping and lifting size constraints, use overflow:auto for deliberate scroll areas with keyboard access, and avoid overflow:hidden when it would clip content, focus rings or menus.
